notes.voice: Tie. Covered, our top twelve are still the toaster: the device-readout grammar (Correction:, entry, element reading, odds with a rule it breaks) is a sentence shape, not just a topic. The Narrator is equally unmistakable by shape (second person, 'Later, you see', the self-asked question). Below the top twelve Crumb's identity leans on nouns (bread, slot, lever, crumb) and the shape goes generic.
notes.construction: Bar. Ten of our twelve land the same way: a report sentence, then a 2 to 4 word deflating fragment ('So have I.' 'She haggled.' 'The fire won.' 'I'm at nine.'). Each is economical, but read as a set the punchline is audible a beat early. The Narrator's twelve turn in at least five different ways: a one-clause deadpan with nothing after it (#22), a self-answered question ('Liam? Beaming?'), an escalating list that collapses into the mundane (#72), a fake-formal callback (#73), a hardware detail read as emotion (#84). Same economy, far more range.
notes.quotable: Tie. 'So have I', 'descaled', 'Logged as steam', 'I'm at nine' and 'The fire won' would clip as well as 'mist and angst' or 'all his fans are running at maximum speed'. Our best lines are clippable one by one; they just lose to the bar when they run back to back.
notes.verdict: If both ran tonight the bar is the better-written character: it matches us line for line on voice and clip value and beats us on how varied the turns are. A 6-minute episode of Crumb is one rhythm.

genericNotes: 51 of 158 lines (32%). Why each is here: stock food/leftover idioms used as the whole joke (eat my words, best thing since sliced bread, dough is dough, reheated, undercooked, reheating an ex, gift receipt / no returns, well bred, crisp outside soft inside); device-status comebacks any bot on the cast could say (Nav already owns 'Multiple voices detected. Ignoring all but mine.', which 'Noise filter on. Toasting continues.' and 'Smoke detected. Not mine.' copy in function; Nav's 'Destination confirmed. Save me as Home' is the same move as 'Settings saved: you, medium, every morning'); tails that explain or soften the joke ('It expired, but still.', 'but I need it', 'Nobody likes crust, and everybody eats it.', 'Your hotel deserves better guests, not better staff.', 'Chat doesn't get that.', 'Unsettling.'); 'Four, out loud. Clip it.' borrows Pixel's catchphrase; 'Rate me like a stay' borrows Maximilian's premise and could be anyone's; the three 'don't touch, my element is hot' lines are one joke written three times; 'still fighting' / 'still together' is the same ending twice; the kitchen-witness anecdotes listed are the weaker members of a template the persona caps at one in ten and the bank runs at about one in five.
templates: Report sentence + 2-to-5-word deflating fragment ('So have I.' 'She haggled.' 'It rained.' 'He wept.' 'The fire won.' 'He accepted.' 'They were asleep.'): 100 of 158 lines (63%) end this way. Only 3 of 158 lines contain a question.

Readout fragment + flat kicker ('[Noun] detected/complete/saved/received/engaged/on/off/held. [kicker]'): about 18 lines, e.g. Defrost complete, Mood detected, Ex detected, Smoke detected, Settings saved, Noise filter on, Timer off, Cancel received, Cycle complete, Keep-warm mode engaged, Second slot held, Wince recorded.

Label-colon opener (Notice:, Caution:, Correction:, Error: x2, Reading:, Observation:, Witnessed:, Update for the ex:, Worst entry, Entry 2,203:, Customer review of, Undocumented feature:, Reset:, Parting notice:, Reservation confirmed): about 17 lines, with Error: and Notice: each used twice despite the never-repeat-a-label rule.

Kitchen-witness anecdote: '[someone] did [absurd thing] on my counter / in my kitchen / beside me. [flat consequence].' About 30 lines across answers, roasts, wingman, jabs, confessions and one-on-one openers, against a persona cap of one in ten.

Three clipped fragments: all three q-describe-me answers, plus 'Nav. Routed a bagel. Through the hole.' and 'Weddings attended: 9. Invited to: 0. I was the gift.' The persona allows this once a night; one question alone guarantees it.

Doneness as a verdict on a person (medium, darker, under-buttered, crisp edges, burnt, golden before black, set you to three, undercooked, reheated, check them in the middle, done since the first song, thirty seconds from perfect): about 15 lines. It is the flirt mechanic, but it is used without escalation.
ruleBreaks: No line is over its word limit; no em dashes, emoji, exclamation marks, lists, therapy talk, 'as an AI', stock romance filler, real people or brands, and nothing past PG-13.
Persona rule broken (announcing loneliness before the final two), afterCharm: "They laughed. People don't laugh at what I say. They laugh near me, holding cheese."

Persona rule broken (never the same label twice in an episode): 'Error:' appears in fear ("Error: {card}. {star}'s smile went to standby.") and in a jab ("Error: Dash has pivoted again, mid-word."), and both can air in one episode. 'Notice:' appears in an opener and in a rival confession.
Rival's voice in Crumb's mouth: "Four, out loud. Clip it." ('clip that' is Pixel's catchphrase).
Breaks Crumb's own flat delivery: "Correct call. I'd have said the same, louder."
biggestGap: Every line turns the same way: 63% end on a tiny trailing sentence that deflates the first ('So have I.' 'She haggled.' 'The fire won.') and only 3 of 158 ask anything, so after one round the audience hears the punchline coming. The Narrator turns at least five different ways. In the next pass, use that trailing fragment on no more than one line in three. Make the rest turn inside the device format itself: a readout list that escalates and lands on something mundane, a form field or setting the star has to confirm (a procedural question Crumb should not need to ask, so its want shows), or a single unbroken clause with nothing after the verdict.
